_readme: Golden canonical entry-hash payloads for certified state transitions (CertifiedTransitionBuilder). The entryHash is what StateLogVerifier recomputes for every entry in an attested state log, so these bytes decide whether a log written yesterday still verifies today. Pinned here and read by the in-repo golden test; the netstandard2.0 probe (scripts/ns20-canonical-bytes-probe.sh) and the .NET 9 probe (scripts/portability/net9-probe.sh) read the entryHash of every case through the public ComputeEntryHash, which is the cross-target byte check those targets can make. To regenerate a case deliberately, copy the actual payload the failing test prints into this file. Regenerate ONLY when the canonical form is deliberately changed, and understand that changing it breaks every attested state log already written. Note that a Base64 field value containing '+' is escaped as a six-character sequence by the default JavaScript encoder while '/' and '=' are not - which is why real Base64 state hashes appear here.

cases.name: transition-genesis
cases.why: The first entry in a log: prevEntryHash is the empty genesis value, pinning that an empty string is written as an empty string rather than omitted or nulled. The behaviour certificate hash is real Base64 carrying a '+', which the encoder escapes.

cases.name: transition-chained
cases.why: A linked entry: every one of the five members carries a distinct non-empty value, and the resulting state hash carries both '/' (not escaped) and '+' (escaped).

cases.name: transition-escaping
cases.why: Non-ASCII, a control character, a surrogate pair, a tab, and every character the default JavaScript encoder escapes - in the action, which is the one member a caller supplies freely. Pins the encoder and its uppercase hex.
